title: Bi dakka, kanka
goal: Recognize the everyday reductions of speech, and use informal words and texting abbreviations with the right people.

intro.text: Short words shrink in speech: *bir* becomes *bi*, *ne haber* becomes *n'aber*, *değil mi* becomes *di mi*, *bayağı* becomes *baya*. Friends also use informal words (*kanka*, *harbiden*, *valla*) and, in messages, abbreviations (*slm*, *tmm*, *tşk*). Keep them for people you say *sen* to.

vocab.en: thanks; OK, fine (informal, mostly between men)
what's up?, is something wrong? (at an unexpected call or visit)
quite, really (spoken: baya); as an adjective: vulgar, common
What's up? How's it going? (spoken: Ne haber?)
right, isn't it (a tag at the end of a question; spoken: değil mi)

exercises.question: *Konser baya güzeldi.* What does *baya* mean here?

why.1: As an adjective before a noun, *bayağı* can mean **vulgar**, but before another adjective *baya* is an adverb: **really, quite**.

exercises.explain: *Baya* is the spoken *bayağı*, an adverb meaning **quite, really**: *baya güzeldi*, it was really good.

exercises.en: Mate, seriously? I can't believe it!
exercises.explain: *Harbiden mi?* is the informal *Gerçekten mi?*, **seriously?** *Eyvallah* thanks or agrees; *hayırdır* asks what has happened.

accept: Is something wrong? Why are you calling at this hour?
Is something wrong? Why are you calling at this hour of night?
Is something wrong? Why are you calling at this time (of night)?
Is something wrong? Why are you calling me at this [hour|time] (of night)?
What is [up|wrong|the matter|going on]? Why are you calling (me) at this [hour|time] (of night)?
Is everything [OK|okay|all right|alright]? Why are you calling (me) at this [hour|time] (of night)?
Has something happened? Why are you calling (me) at this [hour|time] (of night)?
exercises.explain: *Hayırdır*, literally **it's for the good**, asks what has happened when something unexpected does, such as a call late at night.

exercises.question: Who would you call *kanka*?
options: a close friend your own age

why.2: A stranger serving you is *abi*, *abla* or, more politely, *beyefendi* or *hanımefendi*.
why.3: To an older relative, use the family word: *babaanne*, *anneanne*, *nine*.

exercises.explain: *Kanka* (from *kan kardeşi*, blood brother) is for close friends of either sex, mostly among young people.

reject.why: Spoken spelling. In writing: *Bir dakika bekler misin?*

exercises.hint: In speech you'd hear *Bi dakka bekler misin?* Write the first word in standard spelling.
exercises.explain: *Bi* is *bir* without stress. In writing it is always *bir*, and *dakka* is *dakika*.

accept: Honestly, I do not know, ask her.
Honestly I do not know ask him.
I swear I do not know ask [him|her].
Really I do not know ask [him|her].
To be honest I do not know ask [him|her].
Seriously I do not know ask [him|her].
[Honestly|Really|To be honest] I have no idea, ask [him|her].
exercises.explain: *Valla* (from *vallahi*) is emphasis, like **honestly**; *bilmiyom* is the spoken *bilmiyorum*.

exercises.question: In which situation is *Eyvallah!* natural?
options: thanking a friend who held the door
thanking your manager in a formal email

why.1: In a formal email, write *Teşekkür ederim*.
why.2: *Eyvallah* isn't a greeting, and it is too casual for a teacher.
why.3: To apologize, say *Kusura bakmayın* or *Özür dilerim*.

exercises.explain: *Eyvallah* is a casual **thanks** or **OK**, mostly between men who know each other.
*Di mi?* is *değil mi?* as it is said: a tag like **right?** *De mi* asks **… too?** (*Sen de mi?*).

exercises.title: Sınıf grubu
exercises.passage:
**Selin:** slm millet, yarınki sınav kaçta?

**Emre:** 10'da. Harbiden unuttun mu?

**Selin:** Valla unutmuşum. Tşk kanka.

**Deniz:** Bi de hoca ödevleri istiyo, di mi?

**Emre:** Aynen. Yarın getirmeyenin notunu düşürcekmiş.

**Selin:** Tmm. Herkese kib, yarın görüşürüz.
exercises.translation: Selin: Hi everyone, what time is tomorrow's exam? Emre: At 10. Seriously, you forgot? Selin: Honestly, I had. Thanks, mate. Deniz: And the teacher wants the homework too, right? Emre: Exactly. Apparently he'll lower the grade of anyone who doesn't bring it tomorrow. Selin: OK. Take care, everyone, see you tomorrow.

questions.q: What does Selin mean by *Valla unutmuşum*?
options: Honestly, I'd forgotten (I've only just realized)
questions.explain: *Valla* adds honest emphasis; `-mIş` in the first person is a discovery about yourself, as with *meğer* ([C1 unit 7](gp-meger)).

questions.q: According to Emre, what will happen to anyone who doesn't bring the homework?
options: The teacher will lower their grade
questions.explain: *Düşürcekmiş* is *düşürecekmiş*: the spoken future with `-(y)mIş`, passing on what he heard.

exercises.task: Your friend Deniz texts you: *N'aber kanka? Bu akşam maç var, geliyo musun?* Reply as you would text back, casually: say you can't come and why, and suggest another day. Use at least two spoken forms and one informal word or abbreviation.
models: Valla gelemiyom kanka, yarın sabah sınavım var, çalışmam lazım. Cumartesi bi kahve içelim mi? Ben ısmarlıcam!
Slm! Bu akşam olmaz, annemlere gidiyoz. Harbiden çok isterdim ama. Haftaya beraber izleriz, di mi? Tmm, görüşürüz.
checklist: At least two spoken forms: *-yo*, *-icem* or *-cem*, *bi*, *di mi*…
A reason, and a new suggestion
`mI` and *dA* still written apart, as in standard Turkish
